entities.rationale: Rich, neutral and well governed, so collapse risk is mostly global doom plus a European war or energy shock; near-free essentials need superintelligence to break rising health costs from aging.
Among the safest and richest places, with low debt and strong institutions; abundance hinges on superintelligence cutting a health bill that is already over a tenth of GDP.
Basic services are solid, but dependence on Russia, exposure to a Russia-NATO war and an unstable succession after Lukashenko drive the risk; weak governance limits abundance.
Very poor, food insecure and climate exposed, with a recent civil war and weak state capacity; famine or renewed conflict is the main path to collapse and abundance is remote.
Jihadist spillover from the Sahel into the north, a closed dynastic regime and fast population growth make insecurity and food the key risks; low income keeps abundance unlikely.
Politically stable with plentiful hydropower, but heavy external debt, weak health and water systems and Mekong climate stress could erode food and health access.
Severe water stress on a shrinking Amu Darya, a gas economy facing the energy transition and an opaque autocracy with existing food shortages make water and food the weak points.
Rich and efficient but dependent on the mainland for water, food and power, so a US-China war over Taiwan is the main risk; extreme aging pushes health costs up unless superintelligence cuts them.

A divided state with rival governments, extreme water stress on fossil aquifers and an oil income that the energy transition will shrink; renewed civil war or water failure is likely enough to dominate.
Repeated upheavals, border clashes and dependence on remittances from Russia, plus glacier loss threatening water and hydropower, set a moderate risk; low income limits abundance.
A food exporter with abundant hydropower and no water stress, so collapse needs a security breakdown from organized crime; weak health and water services hold back abundance.
A repressive regime facing a fragile succession, high hunger and hurricane exposure make civil conflict and food the main risks; poverty and isolation keep abundance unlikely.
Middle income and food secure, but Kosovo tensions, political unrest and fast aging add some risk; abundance needs superintelligence gains to reach a non-EU, mid-governance state.
An oil state with very weak governance, high debt, widespread hunger and a history of civil war; falling oil income could trigger state failure, so abundance is remote.
EU and NATO membership and low debt keep collapse risk near the global floor; depopulation, Black Sea exposure and weaker governance keep abundance below western Europe's.
Security gains rest on one strongman's crackdown and could reverse, while rising water stress in the Dry Corridor and a heavy interest burden threaten food and water.
Superb state capacity and very high income make it a prime abundance candidate, but it imports almost all food and energy, so a regional war cutting shipping lanes is the main risk.
Rich, cohesive and food exporting, with risk mainly from global doom or a Baltic war; near-free essentials need superintelligence to offset health and rising defence costs.
Already in financial and state collapse, with grid power replaced by private generators, maximum water stress and recurring war with Israel; another prolonged conflict is quite likely.
Among the poorest countries, with over a third undernourished, a weak state and a civil war in living memory; famine or renewed conflict dominates and abundance is very unlikely.
